clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within months: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to your mother's every evening after work; your father took night shifts and distanced from your mother; your uncle Anton's drinking worsened and he separated from Celeste; your mother's anxiety rose over Anton; and your brother Callum's ear infections began that winter. The period settles as your grandmother took a job at the library by May 1979 and began functioning again.

clusters.name: Odette's difficult pregnancy, 1984–1985
clusters.reason: Around your mother being ordered to bed for her pregnancy in March 1984, within months: your grandmother Hazel came every morning to keep house and overfunctioned; your father argued with his mother over how she kept it; your brother Callum stammered again; and you could not sleep without your father by your bed. Your sister Ines was born in September 1984, and the shifts settled within weeks.

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1996
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's diagnosis with Parkinson's disease in September 1986, over the following years: your grandfather Ambrose overfunctioned in her care; your father phoned his father every night and later argued with his uncle Lyle over who should help; your grandfather developed chest pains; Hazel's functioning declined through falls and loss of independence; your father's drinking worsened; your aunt Pearl's anxiety rose; and your father and mother fought over his evenings at his parents' house. The period settles when Hazel moved to the nursing home in June 1997.

clusters.name: Callum's move north, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum leaving home for work up north in May 1999, within months: your father and Callum argued over his plans; your mother's anxiety rose and she could not settle; your father's functioning fell as he missed work and sat in the garage; your sister Ines's functioning fell as she skipped school; and your mother took Ines with her everywhere. The period settles as Ines returned to school full days and passed her exams by August 2000.

clusters.name: Hazel's death, 2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's death in January 2003, within months: you could not sleep more than a few hours a night; you stopped going to the bookshop and were let go in May; you dreaded buses and crowded shops and went out only after dark; and you took a job at the garden centre where you began sleeping through the night again. Every shift in these months is yours, and no one else's shows then.
